Module: invoice Sub-modules: create invoice, send invoice, delete invoice, add lines, etc

This really helps showing what is going on, the good, the bad and the ...you know.

So now it's ready to share. It covers chapter analysis, character overviews, metrics, charts, color spectrums, panel grids, page-by-page detailed notes on themes, symbols, composition, and plot. There are also some longer form essays that go deeper into larger topics.

I hope you like it.

story_text.value:
My cofounders and I are in the process of spinning up an AI integration lab, and over the last year we've consumed billions of tokens across multiple American, European, and Chinese models as a force multiplier for building out our products. However, despite our extensive technical expertise, we've still discovered there are long-term ramifications to heavy agentic AI usage. So I decided to run an experiment for us: given a specification, can an LLM fully, concretely, and correctly implement an internally consistent, linearizable distributed system to the same quality as a human?

This repository is the outcome and showcase of that experiment, complete with the entire session history, including tool outputs. To make this project, I only gave the LLM the AMQP 0.9.1 specification and a few requirements: it must use clustered Raft, and it must support up to 9 nodes (light ceiling, but not the final limit). I picked an older but less well-known protocol as it provided a simplistic base with a wide range of features built on top; a messaging platform more than just a broker. While the specification itself is fairly old, it is still very viable and valuable today for a wide range of uses.

For our uses, I chose Switchboard as the experiment as our products are sealed appliances and we need a stable, scalable message broker that's embeddable into our existing apps (embedded distributed systems are easier when it's all the same binary), deployable as a standalone service, and understandable enough by everyone that debugging and diagnosing it is easy. This experiment is not designed to compete with RabbitMQ or other solutions (altho it is a love letter to my former vmware/Pivotal coworkers who worked on RabbitMQ), and I will be maintaining it for our own use cases.

I wrote it in Rust specifically because our code base is written in Rust. While I may talk about the hands-on design, build, and testing of the project as "automated" and "with long horizon capabilities", it is not vibe-coded slop. There are hundreds of cross-platform and cross-architecture tests, and full Jepsen linearization tests on Linux - I am going to put this software into high-compliance production environments and I need it to be stable.

In finality, I hope you find my little experiment in automated, spec-driven, long-horizon builds interesting and insightful. Contributions are welcome, if desired, but with the age of the protocol I don't expect any real consumers other than our lab.

Happy message passing!

title.value: Show HN: An experiment in automated long-horizon builds with AMQP 0.9.1

I've had the domain for a while as a someday-maybe and figured I had to jump onto the bandwagon! Partly as a challenge to stop navel gazing and ship something. Started yesterday morning, had a chat with ChatGPT on the bus, cleaned up last night and this morning.

I wanted to maximise the Cloudflare static caching and not fiddle too much with security, so it's 400-ish data chunks and each repo should have a stable hash. I only use everything down to 10 mentions since the long tail is long. Might revisit that later, but this gets me published.

Using Google BigQuery and GCP a lot, Jev for classification, Codex as an agent with GPT-6.1 Sol High.

story_text.value:
I'm Alvaro, one of the founders of Mago. With my co-founder Alex (creator of Warpfusion, open source video to video), we built an open source AI video studio specialized in long form content and large volumes of video.

It's a desktop app that you can run for free on your own GPU, that uses a portable ComfyUI or can be plugged into an existing Comfy setup. It handles both hybrid production (video to video, AI VFX) and full AI (microdramas, AI series for social etc).

Back when Alex was working on Warpfusion, we were discussing making an app for "real" production, meaning hours of video, films, series, etc. We started off building a closed source solution, but we're now going back to our roots.

In short: there's a billion AI video tools and it seems like everyone wants to make their own, in fact with the progress of LLMs I'm more and more convinced by the idea of personal software. AI series for TikTok and VFX on a feature film have completely different needs.

AI video is also quite expensive still, unless you can run it on your own GPU. So not only can you run models for free, if the app is open you can also fork it into whatever you want!

Finally, we've been hearing for more than a year that Comfy can be a little too complex, so we thought, well why not try and make open source plug and play? That's the end goal.

Limitations: you'll need an Nvidia GPU with 16GB+ of VRAM and 60GB+ of disk space to host the models (Qwen, Minimax H3). License is AGPL. You can also use closed source models with a Mago subscription.

Please try it out and let me know what we should add next!

title.value: Show HN: Mago, an open source AI video studio, runs locally with Comfy

story_text.value:
I trained a tiny 14M-parameter world model of 2D Minecraft in <10 minutes on 1xA100 (~10 cents on google colab). It runs locally in your browser, so you can play on your phone. It requires WebGPU: Chrome, Edge, or Safari on iOS 26 (built a custom runtime to save memory).

There's also a benchmark to score your own models: beat 0.562 and the site switches to your model. Memory is the open problem: walk 10 tiles away from your table and back, and it's gone.

story_text.value:
Hey HN,

For a while I've building a centralised early warning platforms. Looking everywhere in market watching people build AI chief of staff which does everything for you.

But that lacks few key thing - what's condition of market or what's going on outside. Just based on your data it makes decisions for you which could be painful more often than not.

So I've been building this platform which analyses your data up against market and will warn only if something worth looking if something mismatches.

So what does that means for you? AI provides information to make decisions and you'll be making those decisions.

Working on it - just a demo and haven't published yet, soon will!

Feedbacks are welcome :)
